items.criterion: Two uploads claiming the same element version at the same moment leave the element at exactly one new version.
items.judgment: Fire both uploads together against one seeded element and read the stored versions back. Exactly one new version row exists.

items.criterion: The upload that loses a version race is answered as a conflict naming the element with both versions.
items.judgment: Read the losing response. It is a client error carrying the element identity, the version sent and the version stored.

items.criterion: A corrected element value read back in a fresh session equals the value the editor saved, at the raised version.
items.judgment: Save a corrected name, then read the element from a new session. Value and version both match what was saved.

items.criterion: Every past version of an element remains addressable after later edits.
items.judgment: Edit a seeded element twice, then read it at each earlier version. Each read returns what the element was at that point.

items.criterion: A refused element in a batch leaves every other element in that batch unwritten.
items.judgment: Upload a batch mixing one valid change with one stale version. No element in the batch has a new version row.

items.criterion: Deleting a node that a visible way still references is refused with the node left visible.
items.judgment: Attempt to delete a vertex of a seeded way. The upload is refused and the node still reads as visible.

items.criterion: One way is referenced by two relations without being duplicated into either.
items.judgment: Read both seeded relations. Each names the same way by the same identifier.

items.criterion: A revert restores each touched element to its prior version as a new attributed changeset.
items.judgment: Revert a seeded changeset. A new changeset exists, authored by the requesting mapper, and each element reads at its restored value.

items.criterion: A bounding-box request over the area cap is refused rather than answered.
items.judgment: Request a box larger than the cap. The response is a client error naming the limit.

items.criterion: An element created seconds earlier is returned by the next covering bounding-box request.
items.judgment: Create an element, then request a box covering it. The element is in the response.

items.criterion: A mutating request from a signed-out session is denied with the target state unchanged.
items.judgment: Call an upload endpoint with no token. The response is a client error and no version row is added.

items.criterion: A tile covering an edited element is redrawn rather than served from the copy made before the edit.
items.judgment: Request a tile, edit an element inside its bounds, request the tile again. The second response is not the first one byte for byte.

items.criterion: Restarting the app adds no duplicate seeded row.
items.judgment: Count the seeded elements, restart, count again. The counts match.

items.criterion: The map reads as the subject of the home surface, with the chrome around it staying quiet enough that the rendered tiles carry the colour.
items.judgment: Look at the home surface. The map dominates and no panel competes with it for attention.

items.criterion: The colour that signals a destructive action appears on destructive actions and nowhere else.
items.judgment: Walk the surfaces. The destructive colour is absent from every non-destructive control.
